title: Quant-aware kernel arbitration with staggered prefill and lazy dequant
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Background: Dequantization overhead and suboptimal kernel selection for mixed-precision workloads are a measurable source of latency and cost when serving quantized models (INT8/FP8 + mixed precision fallback). Current runtime heuristics pick kernels mostly based on model architecture and static seq len thresholds, which leads to frequent full-buffer dequant passes during prefill and decode transitions. This ticket proposes a quant-aware arbitration layer that factors per-request quant metadata and a staggered prefill schedule to minimize synchronous dequant stalls.

Goals: (1) Reduce wall-clock dequant overhead for typical chat workloads (variable prefill length followed by short decodes). (2) Improve kernel selection accuracy for mixed-precision paths so the runtime favors quant-friendly microkernels when beneficial. (3) Avoid regressions for long-prefill/high-throughput scenarios.

Proposed approach:
- Add per-request quant metadata (quant_type, scale-shape, per-tensor flags) propagated in the request context so kernel selector can prefer INT8/FP8 friendly kernels when metadata matches.
- Implement a lightweight runtime cost model (microbench table) that stores sequence-length x batch-size x quant-path latencies for candidate kernels on each hardware class; update periodically from perf jobs.
- Introduce "lazy dequant": defer full-tensor dequant until the decode boundary when safe, performing minimal on-the-fly dequant of active KV slices required for the current decode window.
- Staggered prefill scheduling: when many prefill requests arrive, schedule KV materialization in staggered windows to avoid a storm of simultaneous dequant passes; combine with opportunistic small-batch decoding to keep tails warm.
- Fallback policy: if microbench estimate predicts no win or if quant metadata is incomplete, fallback to current mixed-precision path to preserve correctness.

Why unique: This combines runtime-aware kernel arbitration (not just static rules) with an operational prefill scheduling pattern and a lazy-dequant execution model to reduce synchronous stalls at the critical prefill->decode handoff.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end p50 latency for short-chat scenario (avg prefill 64 tokens, decode 16 tokens) improves by >=20% on INT8 path; p95 does not regress by more than 5%.
2) Dequant CPU/GPU memory copies measured per request drop by >=50% for qualifying quantified workloads.
3) Kernel selector accuracy (choose quant-friendly kernel when microbench predicts benefit) >= 90% on validation trace set.
4) No correctness regressions across model-suite (causal/gpt-style and encoder-decoder smoke tests).
5) Deployment gated by canary traffic with monitoring dashboards showing cost and latency trends.
test_plan:
- Create synthetic trace sets: short-chat (prefill 32-128 tokens + decode 8-32 tokens), long-prefill (512+), and high-concurrency bursts.
- Microbench harness to populate per-hardware microbench table (A100, H100, T4 equivalence).
- Unit tests for quant metadata propagation and selector decision logic.
- Integration tests exercising lazy dequant slices and correctness for KV reuse.
- End-to-end perf runs on staging cluster with 12h steady-state load and 1h burst windows.
- Canary rollout to 5% traffic for 48h with rollback on error or SLA breach.
benchmark_results: 2026-02-28: microbench on H100: INT8 microkernel (tiling=64) 1.8x faster than FP16 kernel for seq<=128 at batch=1
2026-03-05: staging perf (prototype): short-chat p50 improved 27% vs baseline for INT8 path; p95 improved 3%
2026-03-08: memory copy profiling: avg dequant memcpy time per request reduced 62% in lazy-dequant prototype (measured on pooled-prefill scenario)
implementation_notes:
- Kernel table format: CSV-backed runtime cache keyed by (hw_class, kernel_id, seq_bucket, batch_bucket, quant_type).
- Selector flow: request arrives -> extract quant metadata -> consult microbench table -> if expected_speedup > threshold && safety checks pass then choose quant-friendly kernel + lazy-dequant plan; else default.
- Lazy-dequant design: maintain sparse KV descriptors; dequant operates on 2D tiles matching kernel tiling; use GPU kernels to do in-place dequant to avoid extra host copies where possible.
- Prefill scheduler: tokenization-based windowing with jitter to stagger large prefill KV commits.
- Backward compat: expose feature flag (quant_arbitrate_v2) and runtime env to control thresholds.
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212 (selector core), /pull/4230 (lazy dequant kernels), /pull/4251 (staggered scheduler)
risks:
- Complexity: new selector + table maintenance increases runtime code surface and ops overhead.
- Edge-cases: models with per-layer mixed quantization may not fit the simple metadata model; requires fallback.
- Microbench staleness: hardware/kernel performance changes could make table entries stale; need periodic rebench and safety margins.
- Debuggability: lazy dequant may complicate memory debugging and OOM reporting.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge gated behind feature flag.
2) Run continuous microbench agent weekly to refresh tables.
3) Deploy to staging cluster; run 12h perf/24h soak.
4) Canary 5% production traffic for 48h with automated rollback on: +5% p95 latency, error rate increase, or CPU/GPU memory spike above threshold.
5) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring.
